about: The epistola of the formulary “Second Sunday after Epiphany” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Brethren: Having gifts differing according to the grace that is given us, whether prophecy, let it be according to the rule of faith; or ministry, in ministering; or he that teacheth, in doctrine; he that exhorteth, in exhorting; he that giveth, with simplicity; he that ruleth, with diligence; he that showeth mercy, with cheerfulness. Let love be without dissimulation. Hate that which is evil; cleave to that which is good. Love one another with the charity of brotherhood; in honor preferring one another. Be not slothful in diligence; be fervent in spirit; serve the Lord. Rejoice in hope; be patient in tribulation; persevere in prayer. Communicate to the necessities of the saints; pursue hospitality. Bless them that persecute you; bless, and curse not. Rejoice with them that rejoice and weep with them that weep. Be of one mind toward one another. Mind not high things, but consent to the humble.

ex.w002: The participle opens a sentence that has no main verb in the Latin. It describes us, the faithful, to whom differing gifts of grace are given. No separate word expresses its subject.
ex.w044: From this word Paul sets out a series of participles without a main verb. Each describes the faithful he addresses and works as an exhortation: hating evil. No separate word expresses their subject, an understood you.
ex.w046: A participle in the series from “Odiéntes” (w044): it describes the faithful Paul addresses, cleaving to what is good. No separate word expresses its subject.
ex.w051: A participle in the series from “Odiéntes” (w044): the faithful Paul addresses are to love one another with brotherly charity. No separate word expresses its subject.
ex.w054: A participle in the series from “Odiéntes” (w044): the faithful are to go before one another in showing honor. No separate word expresses its subject.
ex.w057: The adjective is the predicate of an understood subject, the faithful Paul addresses. The Latin leaves out both the subject and the verb, as throughout the series from “Odiéntes” (w044).
ex.w059: A participle in the series from “Odiéntes” (w044): the faithful Paul addresses are to be fervent in spirit. No separate word expresses its subject.
ex.w061: A participle in the series from “Odiéntes” (w044): the faithful are to serve the Lord. No separate word expresses its subject.
ex.w063: A participle in the series from “Odiéntes” (w044): the faithful are to rejoice in hope. No separate word expresses its subject.
ex.w066: A participle in the series from “Odiéntes” (w044): the faithful are to bear tribulation patiently. No separate word expresses its subject.
ex.w068: A participle in the series from “Odiéntes” (w044): the faithful are to persevere in prayer. No separate word expresses its subject.
ex.w071: A participle in the series from “Odiéntes” (w044): the faithful are to share in the needs of the saints. No separate word expresses its subject.
ex.w073: A participle in the series from “Odiéntes” (w044): the faithful are to pursue hospitality. No separate word expresses its subject.
ex.w089: After “Gaudére” (w081) and “flere” (w084), Paul returns to participles: the faithful are to be of one mind toward one another. No separate word expresses their subject, an understood you.
ex.w092: Like “sentiéntes” (w089), the participle describes the faithful Paul addresses: they are not to set their minds on high things. No separate word expresses its subject.
ex.w095: Like “sentiéntes” (w089), the participle describes the faithful Paul addresses: they are to consent to the humble. No separate word expresses its subject.
